assignmentHtml.task: Research ClickHouse's full CDC mechanics in depth. Investigate: (1) ReplacingMergeTree with version column — how FINAL works at query time, what 'visibility' means; (2) CollapsingMergeTree vs VersionedCollapsingMergeTree tradeoffs; (3) What exactly does 'lightweight delete' leave behind physically? When does it become invisible? What remains after TTL/mutation?; (4) ClickHouse mutations for mass updates — are they atomic? Do they block reads?; (5) The Kafka Connect Sink for exactly-once with Debezium — how does the KeeperMap work, what if offsets are rewound?; (6) Dedup token insert_deduplication_token — how long is the token kept?; (7) What happens on ZooKeeper/Keeper outage — can it still serve queries?; (8) Distributed tables — how does a join across shards behave when data isn't co-located?
assignmentHtml.context: Evidence cutoff 2026-09-16. Workload A: clickstream with late events up to 72 hours, dashboards by product/campaign/minute. Workload B: CDC updates/deletes with final consistency. Workload E: erasure — what physical remnants remain. Workload F: recovery behaviors.
assignmentHtml.expected_output: In-depth ClickHouse dossier covering CDC patterns, dedup mechanics, lightweight delete physical behavior, mutations, Kafka Connect sink specifics, Keeper outage behavior, distributed join semantics, with source URLs.

answerHtml: Comprehensive ClickHouse CDC dossier covering all eight topics, based on official documentation and primary sources.

evidence.snippet: ReplacingMergeTree deduplicates rows during background merges only; queries without FINAL can return duplicates and rows that should be deleted. The version column (ver) determines which row wins: with ver, the max version wins, ties broken by most recent part; without ver, last inserted row from most recent part wins. is_deleted marks rows as deleted (requires ver); default keeps last row even if deleted to ensure future lower-version inserts remain removed. Permanent cleanup requires allow_experimental_replacing_merge_with_cleanup + OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL CLEANUP or forced merges via min_age_to_force_merge_seconds.
evidence.supports: FINAL performs query-time deduplication; 'visibility' means a row is invisible only after merge completes or FINAL modifier applied at query time; version column semantics and is_deleted behavior.

evidence.snippet: VersionedCollapsingMergeTree serves same purpose as CollapsingMergeTree but uses different collapsing algorithm allowing insertion in any order with multiple threads; Version column collapses rows properly even if inserted wrong order. CollapsingMergeTree allows only strictly consecutive insertion. During merge, pairs of rows with same primary key AND version but different Sign are deleted regardless of order. SELECT requires aggregation (sum(Sign), sum(Sign*x) with HAVING sum(Sign) > 0); FINAL modifier works but is inefficient for large tables. Cannot compute min/max aggregates because collapsed states' history is not saved.
evidence.supports: CollapsingMergeTree requires strictly consecutive insertion; VersionedCollapsingMergeTree allows arbitrary order/multi-threading due to version-based collapsing. Both need aggregation or FINAL at read time. Tradeoff: Versioned version has higher storage cost (cancel row copies PK fields) and depends on data consistency.

evidence.snippet: Lightweight DELETE is a mutation marking rows via hidden _row_exists system column (True=existing, False=deleted). Rows physically remain until next merge. SELECT internally adds predicate on _row_exists; granules can be skipped when many deleted. For wide parts only _row_exists rewritten, other columns hardlinked; compact parts fully rewritten. apply_deleted_mask=0 bypasses mask to see physical rows. After merge, deleted rows physically removed and _row_exists column disappears if all values True.
evidence.supports: Physical remnants: masked rows stay on disk with _row_exists=false until merge; invisible immediately after mutation completes; after TTL/mutation-triggered merge they are physically gone and the _row_exists column is dropped.

evidence.snippet: When a mutation is issued, ClickHouse schedules creation of new mutated parts leaving originals untouched until ready; once ready, mutated parts atomically replace originals. They don't block inserts but can overlap with ongoing queries; SELECT during mutation may read mix of mutated and unmutated parts causing inconsistent views. Mutations are totally ordered: apply to data inserted before mutation issued. Cannot be rolled back once submitted; continue after server restarts unless KILL MUTATION.
evidence.supports: Mutations are NOT atomic in the sense of instant full replacement; they are per-part async with atomic swap at completion. They do not block inserts. Reads during mutation see potentially inconsistent views. Totally ordered relative to INSERT timing.

evidence.snippet: Exactly-once achieved via KeeperMap state store with linearizable writes and sequential consistency. Per topic/partition: stores minOffset/maxOffset and BEFORE/AFTER flags. BEFORE set pre-insert, AFTER set post-successful-ack. On restart/rebalance: state NONE → insert; BEFORE + same range → reinsert (dedup absorbs); AFTER + same/contained → drop; overlapping → split and insert only new chunk; contains with BEFORE → DLQ; croppped batches drop offsets < stored min. Invalid states (current max < stored min) throw exception. dedup via replicated_deduplication_window or insert_deduplication_token.
evidence.supports: KeeperMap mechanics: strongly consistent per-topic/partition offset state machine with BEFORE/AFTER flags. Offset rewind requires manual deletion of KeeperMap content for that topic (per https://clickhouse.com/docs/integrations/connectors/data-ingestion/kafka/kafka-clickhouse-connect-sink). Exactly-once relies on Kafka Connect redelivery plus ClickHouse dedup.

evidence.snippet: replicated_deduplication_window default 10000: number of most recently inserted blocks for which ClickHouse Keeper stores hash sums. replicated_deduplication_window_seconds default 3600: hash sums older than this removed even if within window; time relative to most recent record, not wall clock; single record stored forever. insert_deduplication_token tracked per partition, higher priority than data hash.
evidence.supports: Token/block-id retention: replicated tables keep dedup entries for up to 10000 recent blocks AND 3600 seconds (whichever first). Non-replicated tables: non_replicated_deduplication_window default 0 (dedup disabled) unless explicitly set positive (docs show examples using 100).

evidence.snippet: If ClickHouse Keeper unavailable at server start, replicated tables switch to read-only mode. System periodically attempts reconnect. If Keeper unavailable during INSERT or error interacting, exception thrown. After reconnect, compares local data with Keeper expectation, syncs from replicas on minor inconsistency. Broken/unrecognized parts moved to detached subdirectory (not deleted); missing parts copied from replicas. Severe divergence triggers safety mechanism preventing server launch; requires force_restore_data flag.
evidence.supports: Keeper outage: non-replicated tables continue accepting writes and serving queries; replicated tables go readonly (writes fail with exceptions); reads still served locally; distributed DDL stalls. Recovery auto-syncs from replicas; severe cases need semi-automatic restore.

evidence.snippet: Normal JOIN: query sent to remote servers; subquery runs on each to form right table; join performed locally per shard. GLOBAL JOIN: initiator runs subquery for one side, collects into temporary table, passes to each remote server; LEFT/INNER use right table as subquery, RIGHT uses left. distributed_product_mode controls nested subqueries over Distributed tables (deny/local/global/allow).
evidence.supports: When data isn't co-located: normal JOIN broadcasts right table to every shard (expensive for large right tables); GLOBAL JOIN computes right side once at initiator and broadcasts to all shards. Collocated sharding on join key allows efficient local IN/JOIN.
